structure.purpose: Scoped agent procedures; judgment stays here rather than in shell glue.
Repository-wide operational harness and deterministic support code.
First Mate interoperability probes and the crew-orchestration harness.
Machine/device profile harnesses such as Android/Termux; separate from laptop crew readiness.
Portable deterministic contract and completeness tests.
Repository validators and operator entrypoints, primarily PowerShell.

commands.build: No product build is owned by this harness; run the selected project validator after a crew task.
commands.deploy: Not owned. This harness grants no deployment or live-target authority.

known_traps: Linux aarch64 availability is not Android/Termux proof.
Herdr is not a project manager; it is a session backend candidate.
First Mate is not the AgentSwitchboard control plane; it is a crew orchestration candidate.
Android readiness does not block productive laptop/WSL crew work; the lanes are independent.
Do not infer a valid Git checkout by requiring .git to be a directory; linked worktrees use a .git file.
Normalize equivalent GitHub origin transports before comparing repository identity.
Do not auto-promote Herdr while its pinned contract and live runtime gates are unresolved.
Do not use First Mate remote-writing modes until the local-only runtime gate has evidence.

Do not feed Windows temporary paths through wslpath and then parse combined native output; launch wsl.exe with the exact Windows worktree as ProcessStartInfo.WorkingDirectory and capture stdout/stderr separately.
A WSL configuration warning on stderr is diagnostic evidence, not machine-readable path or JSON output.
